_doc: Linux systems the DayZero builder can put on a USB stick (builder/lib/Linux.psm1, Resolve-DzLinuxIsoSource).
baseUrl:     official HTTPS download folder. Only hosts in allowedHosts are accepted (tests check this).
latestFrom:  {page, regex}: the current release as named on the project's own page (regex group 1 = {v}).
latestDir:   regex: take the highest-numbered folder in baseUrl ({v} = its name).
path:        added to baseUrl after that ({v} filled in).
sums / sumsPattern: the checksum file (name, or regex over the folder listing). sha256sum and BSD styles.
isoPattern:  regex for the ISO name inside the checksum file ({v} filled in); the newest match wins.
The ISO must match the published SHA-256, byte for byte, or it is thrown away.
The checksum always comes from baseUrl's host. The ISO itself may be redirected (https only)
to the project's mirrors (Debian does); the checksum still decides.
automation:  'ubuntu-autoinstall' = DayZero writes autoinstall.yaml + the Linux kit (kit/linux);
the disk screen ALWAYS stays interactive: DayZero never picks, wipes or partitions a disk.
'none' = the ISO is written to the stick as it is (like Rufus DD mode) and read back.
largestFile: (FAT32 copies only) biggest single file seen in the ISO (bytes); checked again before erasing.
Any other Linux ISO file can still be written as-is ('raw') with no DayZero automation.
